instruction: Add a new slide at the end titled "Budget Overview", ensuring the title color matches the presentation theme

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a third slide with title 'Budget Overview' in red color (255,0,0) matching the first slide. Verified from analysis: slide 1 title uses RGB(255,0,0).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct title text, 1.0 for correct title text and color

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both instruction requirements: (1) slide title text 'Budget Overview' and (2) title color RGB(255,0,0) matching presentation theme.

RGB color comparison is correctly implemented (slides.py:74-76). Converts python-pptx RGBColor object to tuple before comparison: 'actual_color_tuple = (actual_color.r, actual_color.g, actual_color.b)' then compares with expected tuple.

Title shape detection is properly implemented (slides.py:37-42). First checks for actual title placeholders using 'shape.is_placeholder' and 'placeholder_format.type == 1', with sensible fallback to first text shape.
Partial credit scoring is semantically appropriate: 0.5 for correct title text only, 1.0 for both title text and color matching.
Postconfig correctly activates window and saves file (Ctrl+S), ensuring PPTX is written to disk before get_vm_file retrieves it.
Expected values are semantically correct: slide_idx=2 for third slide (adding 'at the end'), expected_color_rgb=[255,0,0] verified from presentation theme analysis.
Minor edge case: If title has correct text but no runs/paragraphs, returns 0.5 (partial credit). This is acceptable behavior - title exists but lacks formatting.
